source: Fluency Studio: B1 to B2 English Course Syllabus (21 Nov 2026)

course.title: Fluency Studio: B1 to B2 English Course
course.summary: A self-paced British English course in two 16-week stages that takes learners from secure B1 towards B2 in about eight months, with short daily tasks, instant feedback and no fixed class times.
course.audience: Adults and older teenagers (16+) who already use English at B1 level and want to reach B2.
course.disclaimer: The course is preparation for B2. It builds a strong base but does not guarantee a B2 result.
course.start: Start any day. There are no term dates or class times. Sign up, take the placement test and begin straight away.
course.pace: About 3-3.5 hours a week. Sixteen weeks per stage is the recommended pace, not a deadline.

placement.summary: A 24-question test, a short recorded speaking sample and a written paragraph place you at Stage 1 or Stage 2.
placement.belowB1: Learners below B1 are pointed to a foundation course first.

stages.title: Stage 1: B2 preparation
stages.aim: Secure B1 grammar, then the main B2 structures.
stages.grammar: One main and one light point a week.
stages.speaking: Recorded tasks up to 3 min; AI conversation up to 10-15 min.
stages.extraInput: About 60 min a week from the input library.

phases.pronunciationFocus: word stress in featured words and -ed endings
weak forms (was, were, can, have) and contractions
sentence stress on the key information
chunking and pausing in longer turns

stages.title: Stage 2: B2 consolidation
stages.startingLevel: B1+ (Stage 1 finished, or placed at B1+)
stages.aim: Use B2 language accurately and at length, including exam-style tasks.
stages.grammar: One main point a week, extending Stage 1, plus a recycled point.
stages.vocabulary: 8-10 words and 5-7 collocations a week, plus word formation.
stages.speaking: Long turns of 2-3 min with follow-up; 15-min AI conversation and debate.
stages.writing: 220-260 words: essays, reports, reviews, formal emails.
stages.extraInput: About 60 min a week, authentic B2 material.

phases.pronunciationFocus: intonation for questions, lists and polite requests
pace and pausing in a 3-minute long turn

weeklyTasks.title: Vocabulary: new words, collocations and word families
Grammar: the main point and the light point
Speaking task: a recorded answer, model hidden on the first try
Conversation: a spoken exchange with the app's AI partner
Review: your cards, mistakes and saved words
Extra listening and reading from the input library
weeklyTasks.time: About 60 min a week, in any blocks

progression.rule: The next week opens when you have done the speaking task, the writing task, and either the listening or the reading.
progression.details: Do the tasks on any days, in any order; the app suggests an order that works well. Other tasks, including the AI conversation, are recommended: the app shows what you have skipped.
progression.target: Doing at least five tasks and 40 minutes of extra listening or reading each week is a good target.
progression.feedback: Exercises are marked as you answer. Speaking, conversation and writing get feedback within seconds: one specific correction, your errors with a corrected version, and an invitation to try again.

levels.value: Authentic B2, captions off where possible

externalAssessments.title: Starting test
externalAssessments.description: The free EF SET four-skill test (online, about 90 minutes, aligned to the CEFR).

marking.summary: Speaking and writing are marked on how well you complete the task, your vocabulary, your grammar and how clearly you organise your ideas. Feedback is instant; if you study with a teacher, they confirm or adjust it.

certificate: The EF SET shows your progress. If you need formal proof of your level, for example for work or university, you can book Cambridge Linguaskill, an online four-skill test you can take from home, through a test centre. It is paid separately.

principles: You speak and write every week. Each week ends with a speaking task and a writing task, and progress moves on when they are done, together with that week's listening or reading.
Fewer words, learned properly. 8-10 new words a week, each with its key collocation, brought back at the right moments by spaced repetition.
Lots of listening and reading. About an hour a week of extra material on the week's theme, at your level, counts as part of the course.
One grammar point at a time. One main point and one lighter point a week, with a grammar clinic for B1 basics such as articles and prepositions.
Instant feedback. Every task is marked as soon as you submit it, with your mistakes corrected and a chance to try again straight away.
Your mistakes shape your review. Errors you make become review cards, so you practise what you personally get wrong.
Honest about speaking. The app does not score your pronunciation automatically. You shadow model recordings and check yourself; a teacher can assess pronunciation if you study with one.

adaptation.mistakes: Errors from your speaking, writing and exercises are saved and turned into review cards. Mistakes you repeat come back more often.
adaptation.ownWords: While doing extra listening or reading, you can save up to five new words a week with the sentence you found them in. The app adds a definition and British audio.
adaptation.spacedRepetition: Course words, your own words and your mistakes come back just before you are likely to forget them, in about 15 minutes of review a week.
adaptation.grammarClinic: Short refreshers on B1 basics (present tenses, articles, quantifiers, prepositions, subject-verb agreement) whenever your mistakes show you need them.
adaptation.personalReviewWeeks: Weeks 16 and 32 review the grammar you personally find hardest.

aiAndData: You always know when it is AI. AI feedback, AI marks and the conversation partner are clearly labelled. If you study with a teacher, they can confirm or change the AI's feedback.
You can disagree. Tap "I think this is right" on any feedback and it is sent for review where a teacher is available.
Your accent is not a mistake. Feedback is about grammar, vocabulary and clarity; a regional or Spanish accent is never marked as an error.
Your own work. Write inside the app. Checkpoint writing is timed, and answers written by another AI tool will not help you learn and may be reviewed.
A safe conversation partner. It stays on the week's topics, declines inappropriate subjects, and has a report button if anything goes wrong.

Accessible by design. All audio has transcripts or captions. If you cannot record speech, for example because of a speech or hearing impairment, contact support for another way to complete the speaking tasks.
Taking a break. You can pause at any time. When you come back, overdue review is spread over your first few days, not given all at once.
Your data. Recordings, writing and progress are stored under a published privacy policy, with set retention periods, and you can delete your data at any time.
teachers: No homework to set or mark by hand. Give each student a stage; the weekly tasks are already built and marked by the app.
See what each student needs. A dashboard shows each student's progress, most frequent errors with their own sentences, saved words, checkpoint results and test results.

Review only what needs you. The review queue shows only the speaking and writing that needs a teacher's judgement: pieces where the AI is unsure, repeated errors, feedback the student disputes, checkpoint pieces, and a small random sample so you can check the AI's marking. Everything else is accepted with its instant feedback.
Confirm the next step. After each stage, the recommended next step is pre-filled for you to confirm.
Live lessons are optional. Use the dashboard to plan your own lessons around students' errors and themes; the app does not depend on them.
